text:
support_jake: heads up — multiple SEs reporting 504s for hosted inference endpoints since the staged traffic shift. Customer impact: elevated error rates and retry storms, a couple billing alerts triggered. details incoming. :warning:

sre_lead_anya: pulling logs now, thanks. any canary id or rollout id?

eng_oncall_mario: saw this too from monitoring — spike at 19:12 UTC, gateway timeouts and `upstream read` errors. looks like traffic split pushed more to the new routing variant unexpectedly.

support_jake: rollout id rl-2026-03-17-traffic-slice. SEs said requests that include long Authorization headers (JWT ~6kb) fail more often. short tokens OK.

platform_robin: that smells like header truncation at the proxy or LB. we recently flipped a traffic-slice routing change that touches `proxy_max_header_bytes` in the staging template.

eng_oncall_mario: repro on my laptop with curl: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $(python -c 'print(\"x\"*6000)')" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
response: HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout after a stream reset from upstream.

sre_lead_anya: can we get the proxy logs for the failed requests? looking for "header too large" or http2 stream resets. @deploy_bot can you show the recent deploys for rl-2026-03-17-traffic-slice?

deploy_bot: deploy rl-2026-03-17-traffic-slice started 2026-03-17T19:09:02Z, staged traffic weights: old=70% new=30% -> accidentally flipped to old=30% new=70% for region us-east-1 at 19:11:38Z (automated patch).

platform_robin: there it is — automated policy flipped weights. new variant's envoy template has `http.max_header_bytes: 8192`. many JWTs > 8k got truncated, then backend rejects or times out.

billing_clara: billing alerts came from retries/ingest surge and also failed-reporting causing duplicate metering events. we should pause the rollout until we mitigate, customers are already seeing billing anomalies.

sre_lead_anya: mitigation plan: 1) revert traffic weights to old=100% for us-east-1 (immediate) 2) patch proxy template to increase `http.max_header_bytes` to 16384 and roll small canary 3) add a request-len check in front to return 400 for >12k auth headers (fail fast) 4) coordinate with billing to dedupe duplicate events.

eng_oncall_mario: I'm executing weight rollback now. running: `redwoodctl rollout set-weights rl-2026-03-17-traffic-slice --region us-east-1 --weights old=100,new=0`

support_jake: copying customers on the rollback and opening support tickets for billing reviews. any ETA on rollback completion?

deploy_bot: weight rollback executed at 2026-03-17T19:13:05Z, propagation confirmed 19:13:18Z.

platform_robin: once traffic is back, we should still ship the header-size patch — new variant has other perf wins but header limit too low. I'll prepare the template change and a canary with a tighter query sample set.

billing_clara: opening billing incidents for impacted customers and pausing metering ingestion for the 19:11-19:13 window to avoid double charges. will provide ticket IDs shortly.

eng_oncall_mario: postmortem checklist: capture request IDs and sample traces for 504s, record deploy automation flip cause, and add a safeguard that prevents automated weight flips >20% without manual ack.

support_jake: thanks team. I'll update affected customers that we've rolled back and are working on a safe redeploy. :thumbsup:

sre_lead_anya: good job. add me to the billing tickets. starting an incident doc in the incidents repo with timeline and AM/PM owners.

deploy_bot: incident created: INC-2026-1745, incident channel: #incidents-INC-2026-1745.

support_jake: noted, moving to that channel for live coordination.

platform_robin: follow-ups: add test for long auth headers in canary harness, tighten automated flip guard, and ensure deploy docs call out header-size changes.

billing_clara: after dedupe, will send credits where applicable.

eng_oncall_mario: closing loop — metrics show error-rate back to baseline by 19:20 UTC. will keep observing for 2 hours.

support_jake: closing here, continuing in incident channel. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
